we have introduced a framework for consensus and synchronization problems in fuzzy environments, and we have applied it to the field of Critical Infrastructure Protection.

we provide a novel theoretical framework to deal with the consensus and synchronization problems in presence of fuzzy initial conditions, and then we apply it to the field of Critical Infrastructure Protection, in order to provide a shared linguistic estimation of the state, or of the interdependencies, of a given infrastructure, or of a set of infrastructures.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the consensus framework is a powerful tool for representing and solving a variety of distributed estimation problems, and the proposed approach can be applied to the field of Critical Infrastructure Protection.

, when dealing with Critical Infrastructure Protection problems, it is important to consider that the state of the system is not always well-defined, but may be affected by vagueness or ambiguity; in this case, the consensus/synchronization problem can be formulated in a fuzzy framework and the resulting algorithms are able to provide an agreement on the state of the infrastructure, even in the presence of imprecise information.

fuzzy-valued systems can be effectively used to describe, model and solve problems in the field of critical infrastructure protection, where the presence of vagueness and ambiguity is often unavoidable.
